summary: A deterministic Discord voice-channel music bot: /music play|skip|queue|pause|resume|stop, resolving a YouTube URL or search query via yt-dlp and streaming it live into voice with ffmpeg -- no downloads, no LLM involvement in any control decision.
details: /music play joins the invoking user's own current voice channel and refuses ("join a voice channel first") if they aren't in one -- unless a session for that guild is already running, which any command can then control regardless of the invoker's own voice presence.

The upcoming queue persists in Postgres (music_queue) and survives a process restart; now-playing/playback position is in-memory only and does not survive one (lost on a restart or a Discord Gateway reconnect, the last limitation below).
Auto-disconnects immediately when its voice channel empties of humans, and after a configurable idle timeout ([music] idle_timeout_seconds, default 300s) when the queue empties with nothing playing.
design/discord-music/ is the design bundle; R-59/R-60 record the join-rejection and disconnect-timer rules.
limitations: Ships OFF ([music] enabled = false). Also requires [platforms.discord] enabled and a bot token with the applications.commands scope.
YouTube only via yt-dlp; SoundCloud and an official-API source are deferred (design/discord-music/04-deferred.md), each with a stated evidence bar.
No saved/named playlists, no persistent audio library/cache -- only the live session queue.
No Nora agent tools (play_music, etc.) -- slash commands are the only control surface for now; a conversational surface is deferred until slash commands prove insufficient on their own.

A Discord Gateway reconnect drops active voice playback (DiscordAdapter builds a fresh discord.Client per connection attempt, and a voice connection is scoped to the client that opened it) -- known, not auto-resumed.
The yt-dlp/ffmpeg subprocess runs directly on the host, not sandboxed; containerizing it is a deferred hardening pass, not a blocker.

Never smoke-tested against a live Discord bot token/voice channel in this environment -- verified by a full unit/contract test suite (including two races reproduced live against Postgres) and the project's mypy/ruff/lint-imports gate, not by an actual voice session.
